repo_notes.content: Don't over-document the fact that the library is implemented 1:1 in many languages, don't describe the minutae of the differences / attempt to individually document Python, TS, Go, and Rust implementations explicitly. We have thorough hand-written + translated examples and source maps available at https://abxbus.archivebox.io/ already, your job is only to document the main shared shapes and APIs and concepts, using Python by default for pseudocode and examples, and leave one or two sentences maximum to describe differences/exceptional cases when they are significant for specific languages.
repo_notes.author: Maintainer

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to abxbus: what it is, why it exists, key design principles, and how the Python, TypeScript, Go, and Rust implementations relate. Links to all major child sections.

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.purpose: Installation, first event, and minimal working examples in both Python and TypeScript. Covers pip/npm install, defining a BaseEvent subclass, registering a handler, and emitting an event.

pages.title: Supported Runtimes & Language Parity
pages.purpose: Documents which Python versions and JS runtimes (Node, Bun, Deno, browser) are supported, and explains the design goal of behavioral parity between the Python, TypeScript, Go, and Rust implementations. Covers the cross-runtime roundtrip test infrastructure.

pages.title: Core Architecture
pages.purpose: Overview of the fundamental building blocks: EventBus, BaseEvent, EventHandler, and EventResult. Explains how they compose and links to child pages for each component.

pages.title: EventBus
pages.purpose: Deep dive into the EventBus class: constructor options, runtime state, handler registration (on/off), emit, wait_until_idle, stop, and the internal run-loop. Covers both Python (abxbus/event_bus.py) and TypeScript (abxbus-ts/src/event_bus.ts) implementations.

pages.title: BaseEvent
pages.purpose: Explains the BaseEvent model: how to define typed events (Pydantic in Python, Zod in TypeScript), all metadata fields (event_id, event_type, event_status, event_path, event_results, etc.), the completion model (await vs event_completed()), and result access helpers (event_result, event_results_list, first).

pages.title: EventHandler & EventResult
pages.purpose: Documents the EventHandler registration object and the EventResult per-handler execution record. Covers handler metadata (handler_name, handler_file_path), result status lifecycle (pending/started/completed/error), error capture, and the scope-stack execution order inside a handler run.

pages.title: Event History & Memory Management
pages.purpose: Explains the EventHistory subsystem: pending_event_queue vs event_history, max_history_size and max_history_drop retention policies, eviction order, and the find() API for querying past or future events.

pages.title: Concurrency & Execution Model
pages.purpose: Overview of all concurrency controls in abxbus: event scheduling modes, handler execution modes, completion strategies, timeouts, and the queue-jump mechanism. Links to child pages for each topic.

pages.title: Event Scheduling Modes
pages.purpose: Covers the three event_concurrency modes: bus-serial (default FIFO per bus), global-serial (single global slot across all buses), and parallel (unrestricted overlap). Includes the LockManager implementation and semaphore internals.

pages.title: Handler Execution & Completion Modes
pages.purpose: Explains event_handler_concurrency (serial vs parallel handlers for one event) and event_handler_completion (all vs first). Covers how 'first' mode cancels losing handlers and how parallel handlers interact with child event emission.

pages.title: Immediate Execution (Queue-Jump)
pages.purpose: Deep dive into the queue-jump mechanism: how awaiting a child event inside a handler causes it to bypass the FIFO queue, the 'no overshoot' constraint, nested execution chains, and interaction with different concurrency modes.

pages.title: Timeouts & Backpressure
pages.purpose: Documents the three-level timeout hierarchy (bus, event, handler), slow-warning thresholds, EventHandlerTimeoutError, and backpressure behavior under high load (max_history_size + max_history_drop interaction with emit).

pages.title: Retry Decorator
pages.purpose: Documents the retry() decorator/HOF available in both Python (abxbus/retry.py) and TypeScript (abxbus-ts/src/retry.ts): max_attempts, retry_after, backoff, retry_on_errors, semaphore-based concurrency limiting, and multiprocess semaphore support.

pages.title: Event Features
pages.purpose: Overview of higher-level event features built on top of the core bus. Links to child pages covering parent-child tracking, forwarding, find/debounce, context propagation, and the events_suck ergonomics layer.

pages.title: Parent-Child Tracking & Causality Trees
pages.purpose: Explains how abxbus automatically records event lineage (event_parent_id, event_children, event_emitted_by_handler_id), how the log_tree() visualization works, and how lineage is preserved across forwarded buses.

pages.title: Forwarding Between Buses
pages.purpose: Covers multi-bus topologies: how to wire buses together with bus.on('*', other_bus.emit), loop prevention via event_path, result aggregation across buses, and design patterns for service-local vs relay buses.

pages.title: Find Events & Debouncing
pages.purpose: Documents the bus.find() API: past/future/where/child_of options, history-only vs future-wait modes, and how to build debounce patterns (reuse recent work, coalesce concurrent callers, history-first-then-future).

pages.title: Context Propagation
pages.purpose: Explains how abxbus captures and restores ambient context (Python ContextVars, Node/Bun AsyncLocalStorage) at emit time so handlers see the same request-scoped values (request_id, trace context, user_id).

pages.title: events_suck: Ergonomics Layer
pages.purpose: Documents the events_suck module (abxbus/events_suck.py, abxbus-ts/src/events_suck.ts): the wrap() helper that generates method-shaped client APIs over event emit/await, reducing boilerplate at call sites.

pages.title: Integrations
pages.purpose: Overview of the two integration layers: Bridges (transport connectors to external services) and Middlewares (lifecycle hooks). Links to child pages for each.

pages.title: Bridges
pages.purpose: Documents all bridge connectors: Redis, NATS, PostgreSQL, SQLite, JSONL, HTTP, Socket, and Tachyon. Covers the shared bridge interface (emit/on/start/close), setup patterns, and optional dependency installation. Includes the high-performance Tachyon SPSC IPC bridge for same-machine cross-runtime communication.

pages.title: Middlewares
pages.purpose: Documents the EventBusMiddleware interface and all built-in middleware classes: WALEventBusMiddleware, LoggerEventBusMiddleware, SQLiteHistoryMirrorMiddleware, OtelTracingMiddleware, AutoErrorEventMiddleware, AutoReturnEventMiddleware, AutoHandlerChangeEventMiddleware.

pages.title: Language Implementations
pages.purpose: Overview of the four language implementations of abxbus: Python (reference), TypeScript, Go, and Rust. Explains the shared JSON wire format and cross-runtime compatibility guarantees. Links to child pages for each implementation.

pages.title: Python Implementation
pages.purpose: Explains the abxbus Python package layout: core modules (event_bus.py, base_event.py, event_handler.py, event_result.py, event_history.py, lock_manager.py, middlewares.py, retry.py, events_suck.py, bridges.py), optional bridge extras, pyproject.toml configuration, and uv-based build/publish workflow.

pages.title: TypeScript Implementation
pages.purpose: Explains the abxbus-ts build pipeline: ESM/CJS/types outputs, build scripts (build_esm.mjs, build_cjs.mjs), pnpm workspace, optional bridge dependencies (ioredis, nats, pg), and browser compatibility notes.

pages.title: Go Implementation
pages.purpose: Documents the abxbus-go package: EventBus, BaseEvent, EventHandler, EventResult, typed helpers (typed.go), JSONLEventBridge, OtelTracingMiddleware, JSON serialization/deserialization roundtrips, and the roundtrip_cli test utility. Covers what is and isn't yet implemented relative to the Python reference.

pages.title: Rust Implementation
pages.purpose: Documents the abxbus-rust crate: EventBus, BaseEvent, EventResult, the event! macro, EventSpec trait, typed handler registration, HandlerExecutor thread pool, ReentrantLock, and dcontext integration. Covers what is and isn't yet implemented (no bridges/middlewares yet) and the Cargo.toml dependency set.

pages.title: Cross-Runtime Roundtrip & Wire Format
pages.purpose: Documents the JSON wire format shared across all four language implementations, the cross-runtime roundtrip test infrastructure (roundtrip_cli in Go, abxbus-rust-roundtrip binary in Rust), and how to verify serialization parity between Python, TypeScript, Go, and Rust.

pages.title: Package Structure & Build
pages.purpose: Overview of the Python and TypeScript package layouts, build pipelines, and distribution artifacts. Links to child pages for the Python package and TypeScript build details.
